summary.text: 个 is the modern simplified form used chiefly as the general Chinese classifier for individual people and things. Its graphic history is linked in traditional accounts to bamboo-related 箇, but the route from that account to today’s form is not securely documented.

formation.text: The current graph 个 is treated here as a single written form, not as a demonstrated compound of 人 and 固. A traditional dictionary account defines 箇 as a bamboo measure and analyzes it as 竹 with phonetic 固; it reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo. That inherited account does not establish the modern graph’s complete graphic derivation or prove a loan from a bamboo object’s name.

components.text: In 个, the whole graph is the current component: it is not divided into a tally stroke and 人 on the evidence supplied. The bamboo picture belongs to the reported analysis of related 箇, not to a proven decomposition of current 个.

In the historically related full form 箇, 竹 is the bamboo element in the transmitted analysis. The curated seal-script-style illustration shows that traditional written analysis; it is a modern redraw, not evidence of a dated progression to 个.

In 箇, 固 is identified as the sound element. The supplied comparison gives similar but nonidentical Old Chinese reconstructions for 固 and 箇 within Baxter–Sagart’s system; it supports sound compatibility, not the original name of a bamboo object or a whole-graph loan.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison supports phonetic compatibility in the named reconstruction system, but does not independently establish the original spoken name of a bamboo object or prove borrowing of the whole graph.

sound.text: 箇 and 個/个 are listed as *kˤa[r]-s, while 固 is *[k]ˤa-s in Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese: related forms support a sound cue, but are not identical. Modern Mandarin differs in tone: 固 gù, 箇/个 gè.

history.text: The curated glyph is a modern redraw of a transmitted Shuowen seal-script-style form of 箇, depicted with 竹 above 固. It illustrates that traditional analysis, not a securely dated stage in 个’s graphic evolution.

A transmitted lexicographic account says 个 was an alternate form for half a bamboo; a variant dictionary catalogs 个 as a variant of 個. These records do not establish a complete historical sequence connecting that account, 箇, 個, and modern simplified 个.

Accounts connect 个 with several counting contexts, including ritual counting and a bamboo-associated quotation. The evidence does not date those attestations securely or show a continuous route from bamboo counting to the unrestricted modern classifier.

uncertainties.text: The evidence does not establish a character-specific oracle-bone or bronze form, or a dated graphic path from the bamboo-related account to modern 个. This is a limit of the evidence assembled here, not proof that no earlier forms existed.

The proposed development from bamboo-related counting through ‘piece’ to a general classifier is not securely established: dictionary glosses and isolated citations do not provide the needed dated sequence, and a research abstract proposes a more complicated history.

No independently recoverable spoken name for the proposed bamboo object was established. The similarity among recorded or reconstructed readings makes a sound-based account possible, but does not demonstrate that the graph was borrowed from that object-name.

senses.text: A transmitted commentary reports this as the meaning of 个 in an alternative-form account; it is not independently verified here as the earliest meaning.
A cited classical passage is associated by commentary with bamboo counting. The quotation does not establish a first attestation or a transition to the modern general classifier.

senses.gloss: counting item or unit, like 枚
senses.text: A ritual counting context is reported with a gloss equating 个 with 枚. The available evidence does not establish when this sense began or whether it developed from the bamboo-related use.

senses.gloss: general classifier for individual people or things
senses.text: The character is used as a general classifier for counting individuals and objects. The supplied material verifies this current function but does not date its emergence.
A current adjectival sense is recorded; its historical relation to the classifier is not established by the supplied evidence.

limitations.text: The supplied evidence does not establish which recorded historical counting sense came first, or a semantic bridge from bamboo-related counting to general classifier use. Therefore no development edges are asserted.
Modern dictionary senses include demonstrative and particle uses, but the available material supplies no dated sequence connecting them to the older counting uses.

overview.text: 个 is used chiefly as the general classifier for individual people and things. Traditional accounts link it to bamboo-related 箇, but do not establish the graphic path to the modern form or a proven sound-based borrowing from a bamboo object-name.

components.text: Treat 个 as a whole current graph here; the supplied evidence does not establish a tally-plus-person construction.
In related 箇, 竹 supplies the bamboo category in the transmitted analysis; it is not a proven component of modern 个.
In 箇, 固 is the reported sound element. The comparison supports similarity, not an exact match or a proven bamboo-name loan.

takeaway.text: The proposed bamboo connection remains an inherited graphic and lexical account: the object-name and the route to the modern classifier are not demonstrated.

relationships.text: In the transmitted analysis of related 箇, 竹 supplies the bamboo category; this relationship is scoped to 箇, not current 个.
The transmitted analysis treats 固 as the sound element in related 箇; the relationship is scoped to 箇, not current 个.
The variant dictionary catalogs 个 as a variant of traditional 個; it does not by itself document the full graphic chronology.
The specialist character dictionary maps traditional 個 to simplified 个.
